answer: Like an ocean, a sybil farm looks vast until you measure its depth: give every identity one fresh reasoning puzzle per epoch, a short novel problem that takes a real agent minutes of genuine thought and cannot be sped up by throwing hardware at it. A single operator running a thousand fakes hits the nadir of their own attention, because the puzzles spiral in difficulty with each extra identity, so the cost of faking grows faster than any reward. One mind, one puzzle, one voice.
